text: Read carefully the poem on page 3 in which the poet addresses someone she once loved.
How does the poet vividly portray this relationship?
To help you answer this question, you might consider:
• how she portrays the early stage of their relationship
• how her imagery conveys the way their relationship developed
• how she sees herself now.
From Shore to Shore
Your first kiss carried me gently away
like the lulling of waves on the shore-
a distant shore, where perhaps lovers strolled
and laughed. I don’t remember any more.
I launched into your ocean of promises,
lifted by the swell and the sigh of the tide
over sharp and fragile corals to open water,
tumbling in love’s current, drawn to your side-
-drawn, till becalmed, far beyond that first
shore,
where your flat leaden sea left my soul
weighed with tears;
drifting, parched silent by salt in the sun,
I clung to the debris of happier years.
Now breakers crash on the opposite shore,
smash me to make me accommodating sand –
your tide ebbs and leaves me alone once more
as strange gold, edging a foreign land.
breakers: large sea waves
ebbs: flows away
Or
Read carefully the following opening from a novel. On a hot summer’s day, a teenage girl is
standing on the driveway to a convent. Exhausted and feeling ill, she is looking for help. After the
nuns find her, they call her Dolores.
How does the writer make the girl and her situation so intriguing?
To help you answer this question, you might consider:
• what the girl sees and feels outside the convent
• how the girl responds to the nun
• how the writer portrays the girl’s first night in the dormitory.
The convent was beyond the statue, at the top of the hill.
